title: P1-04 — Minimal host metrics parity over identity-bound SSH
objective: P1-04 minimal host metrics parity. Successor to #49/#51; depends on P1-01 ticket #53 evidence context. Design-only assessment may proceed before P1-02 #54; implementation is blocked on Sol review and explicit owner approval, and final acceptance is #57.

acceptance_criteria.text: Before implementation, submit an exact-SHA design packet for Sol combined security/implementation assessment and obtain explicit owner approval of any new host-to-guest data path.

Define a versioned fixed-schema snapshot with bounded numeric values/strings/arrays, UTC sample and receipt timestamps, monotonic freshness marker, explicit unavailable values, and stale threshold; propose 2-second cadence, 1-second collector/push deadline, 16-KiB maximum payload, and 6-second stale threshold for owner approval.

Use only the existing run-scoped identity-bound, host-key-verified SSH capability to push to a fixed guest receiver; no data interpolation into commands, guest-originated host request, listener, new egress, direct /proc-/sys-/device mount, or PID authority.
Receiver validates size/schema/ranges and atomically replaces one private tmpfs snapshot with symlink/special-file protections; UI distinguishes fresh, stale, and unavailable data.

Expose a host-OS-portable collector interface with optional platform/vendor collectors; every executable collector passes existing provenance policy. Current Linux/KVM support is not misrepresented as cross-platform support.
Reuse historical gather/formatter/TUI logic selectively; do not import the Compose HTTP server or its network topology.

needed: Sol design review and owner authorization before code.
Schema bounds, unavailable/stale data, timestamps, atomic replacement, symlink refusal, timeout, overflow, provenance and no-listener/no-new-egress negatives.
Owner hands-on metrics accuracy and stale/unavailable display on the protected interactive guest.
